summary_rationale: PCBL Chemical runs India's largest carbon black franchise, with captive co-generation that turns a by-product into sellable power, a 900 ktpa capacity base and a specialty-chemicals arm bought through Aquapharm. The core carbon black engine works: FY2026 volume was a record, the audited statements are unmodified, receivables are clean and the business stays profitable through the cycle. The group is not a compounder on the evidence so far. Pre-tax ROCE fell from 16-23% before FY2024 to about 8% after the Aquapharm acquisition, and free cash after interest, leases and capex was negative before working-capital swings in FY2025 and FY2026. Aquapharm EBITDA of Rs 162 Cr in FY2026 is well below the Rs 250-300 Cr management guided at signing, net debt stays above 4x operating EBITDA with AA ratings on Negative outlook, the FY2026 dividend exceeded profit, and H1 FY2027 EBITDA is roughly flat once inventory gains and a tariff refund are removed. Management delivered mainly the promises it controls mechanically (volumes, plant ramps) and missed or left unproven most of the Aquapharm, debt and battery-material commitments. The verdict is cyclical and conditional: genuine franchise assets, but cash returns on the recent capital are unproven and depend on Aquapharm recovery, utilisation of new capacity and deleveraging.
